## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind, two independent reviewers per paper (third reviewer if split decision); target 4 months from submission to decision, though special-issue guest editors can extend this; accepted papers typically appear within two issues (~6 months) of acceptance. |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | *(pending)* |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | *(pending)* |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | *(pending)* |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | *(pending)* |

> Source: https://ixdea.org/reviewing-process/

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — WO2 defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Dedicated 'Policy on the use of GenAI' (journal-specific, publisher-hosted). AI use permitted under human oversight for language improvement, content organization, literature synthesis, and figure generation; must not obscure/misrepresent information; authors responsible for verifying accuracy/originality; AI cannot be listed as author/co-author. Mandatory disclosure: authors must submit a 'Use of Generative AI statement' naming tool, version, purpose, and affected sections (minor language/grammar fixes exempt from disclosure). Reviewers barred from uploading confidential submissions to GenAI tools without data-privacy guarantees; human evaluation still required. Guest-editors barred from using GenAI for manuscript evaluation/communications; journal itself may use in-house/licensed AI for plagiarism/formatting checks. Non-disclosure or misuse = breach of publication ethics, risking rejection/retraction. |
| **Source URL** | https://ixdea.org/ixda-policy-on-genai/ |

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** Gold/Diamond OA, no APC. Regular submissions always open alongside rotating special issues. Recent/upcoming special issues (2026-2027) center AI: N.68 'Participatory Design meets Artificial Intelligence' (current), N.69 'Sustainability and Innovation in Creative Industries and Design' (Summer 2026), N.70 'Democratic Technology Design' (Autumn 2026), N.71 'AI enhanced learning ecosystems' (Winter 2026), N.72 'From education to societal wellbeing for all' (Spring 2027). Recent article examples found: AI applied to social mapping of rural music festivals (issue 65), 'AIs @ School' perception study (issue 62), smart learning ecosystems research orientation study (issue 64), AI-and-education grand-challenges preface (issue 59).

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** participatory/co-design studies, qualitative and mixed-methods HCI research, educational technology / technology-enhanced learning studies, social mapping / computational social science applied to design contexts (e.g., ML on cultural/social data), policy and ethics analysis of AI in education/design (e.g., EU AI Act discussions), case studies and perception/survey studies on AI-in-education actors
